- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) followed by true price drop, apply “overshoot correction” — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.  
- If true price deviates from forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, check for mean reversion — adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- When sentiment history includes 2+ positive spikes (e.g., >0.20), model often overreacts — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak if sentiment remains positive.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., -3% avg deviation), apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days if sentiment remains negative.  
- If sentiment is negative but price is rising (e.g., -0.10 sentiment, +2% price move), model may be underestimating momentum — increase forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 days.
